verdict.summary: Any Contentful user can register an OAuth application in account settings and any other Contentful user can authorize it the same day; we found no review or install cap in the docs. The documented flow is implicit-style (response_type=token, token in the URL fragment), with only two scopes, and the token carries the user's full access across all their spaces.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app, set an HTTPS redirect (ngrok for localhost), redirect to be.contentful.com/oauth/authorize, and read the token from the fragment.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent that reads or edits content via the Content Management API on behalf of any Contentful user; a Marketplace App Framework listing is a separate, optional path.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Contentful's OAuth docs describe creating an app and requesting tokens with no review step; absence of review is our reading.

prerequisites.why: OAuth applications are created under your account profile settings.
The redirect URI must be HTTPS; Contentful suggests ngrok during development on localhost.

prerequisites.item: A front-end or redirect page that can read the URL hash fragment
prerequisites.why: The access token arrives in the redirect URI's hash fragment, which isn't sent to your server.

scopeTiers.impact: Read access to everything the authorizing user can see in the Content Management API.
Read and write; includes read, so request only this one if the agent edits content. Writes are limited only by the user's own space roles.

steps.title: Sign in to Contentful
steps.detail: Use or create a Contentful account (a free space is enough for testing).

steps.title: Pick the scope
steps.detail: Choose content_management_read for read-only agents or content_management_manage for editing; request one scope per authorization.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Single-scope requests are reported by a third-party connector changelog.

steps.title: Create the OAuth application
steps.detail: Account settings → OAuth applications → new app: name, description, HTTPS redirect URI, scope checkboxes, and confidential or public client type. Copy the client ID.

steps.title: Build the authorize redirect and callback
steps.detail: Send users to https://be.contentful.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=token&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=content_management_manage and parse #access_token=... on the redirect page, then post it to your backend over HTTPS.

steps.title: Test the consent flow
steps.detail: Authorize with your own account and confirm the agent can list spaces and entries.

steps.title: Add rate-limit handling
steps.detail: Respect the default 7 requests/second CMA limit; on 429 wait X-Contentful-RateLimit-Reset seconds.

steps.title: Handle EU data residency
steps.detail: Route EU data residency customers to https://api.eu.contentful.com for CMA calls.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether EU users use a different OAuth authorize host is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Offer token revocation
steps.detail: Let users disconnect and revoke tokens via the CMA access-token revoke endpoint; track revokedAt.

agentCanDo: Generate the authorize URL and fragment-parsing callback
Route EU-residency customers to the EU API host
humanMustDo: Create the OAuth application in account settings

blockers.symptom: Authorization error on Contentful's consent page
blockers.cause: Requesting multiple scopes in one request, or a scope not ticked on the OAuth app.
blockers.fix: Request a single scope that matches the app's configured checkbox.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From third-party connector docs (Prismatic changelog, StackOne guide), not Contentful's own docs.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI rejected when using http://localhost
blockers.cause: Contentful requires an HTTPS redirect URI.
blockers.fix: Use a tunnel such as ngrok during development.

blockers.symptom: Your server never receives the token
blockers.cause: The token is returned in the URL hash fragment, which browsers don't send to the server.
blockers.fix: Read the fragment with client-side JavaScript on the redirect page and post it to your backend.

blockers.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests during bulk sync
blockers.cause: Default CMA limit is 7 requests per second.
blockers.fix: Throttle and honor X-Contentful-RateLimit-Reset; higher limits depend on the customer's plan.

blockers.symptom: API calls fail for an EU customer
blockers.cause: EU data residency customers use a different base URL.

nuances.text: A CMA token inherits the same access rights as the user's account, so an OAuth token reaches every space and organization that user can access. There are no per-space scopes.
The documented flow returns no refresh token. OAuth tokens appear as OAuthApplication CMA tokens that can be listed and revoked; Contentful's docs don't state a default expiry for them.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Personal access tokens don't auto-expire unless expiresIn is set; we assume similar for OAuth tokens but couldn't confirm.

nuances.text: Content Delivery API (published content) uses separate space-level API keys, not OAuth tokens; OAuth covers the Content Management API.

For space-scoped, backend access, the App Framework (app definitions, app keys and app identities) is an alternative to user OAuth; most of its setup needs organization owner, admin or developer roles.
Contentful publishes Markdown versions of its docs (append .md) and a docs MCP server for AI coding tools.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The .md variant returned 200 on 2026-10-20 while the HTML docs returned 429 to automated fetches.

sources.title: Contentful CMA: Overview (rate limits, EU base URL)
Contentful App Framework: Building a backend app (app identities and events)

tested: https://be.contentful.com/oauth/authorize returned HTTP 200 (with and without dummy parameters; no login attempted)
https://be.contentful.com/.well-known/openid-configuration returned a 'Page Not Found' page, no OIDC discovery
contentful.com HTML docs returned HTTP 429; the .md variants returned 200
openQuestions: Whether Contentful supports an authorization code grant (with refresh tokens) for confidential clients, beyond the documented response_type=token flow
Default lifetime of OAuth application tokens
Whether EU data residency users authorize at a different OAuth host
Whether organizations can block third-party OAuth apps
